cards.text: Grab a seat, friend, because Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing a letter. It goes to people who received their faith through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ. And their faith? Peter's got something to say about it.

cards.question: Peter is an apostle of Jesus. He tells his readers they have received a faith as precious as his.

cards.text: Then comes his greeting: "Grace and peace be multiplied to you…" MULTIPLIED, friend, like a batch that doubles every time I open the oven, and mine has NEVER done that.

cards.question: Peter wants grace and peace multiplied to his readers. Through what?

answers.text: The knowledge of God and of Jesus
The strength of their own effort

cards.text: Now Peter turns to God's divine power, and what it has given us for life and godliness.

cards.question: How much of what we need for life and godliness has God's divine power given us?

cards.text: And it all comes through the knowledge of Him, the One who called us by His own glory and excellence. That word "knowledge" again, friend, two verses in a row.
Through these, He has given us His "precious and magnificent promises". MAGNIFICENT, friend, and nobody has ever said that about "I'll call you right back."

cards.question: Peter's been talking about life and godliness. He says God gave these precious promises for a reason. What is it?

answers.text: So they can share in God's own nature
So they can stay free from hard times
So they can be rewarded with great riches

cards.question: Everything Peter's described so far, God has already given. Peter says these believers are still waiting to escape the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.

cards.text: After all that, Peter writes, "For this very reason, make every effort…" Not snooze-button effort, friend, not "I'll start Monday" effort, EVERY effort.

cards.question: Peter tells his readers to make every effort to add to something they already have. What is it?

cards.text: To their faith, Peter says, add virtue.

cards.question: Peter says that once they add virtue to their faith, they're done adding.

cards.text: And Peter keeps stacking. To virtue add knowledge, then self-control, perseverance, godliness and brotherly kindness, and that is the TALLEST stack of toppings I have ever seen on one cookie.

cards.question: Peter's list climbs one quality at a time. What's the last one he adds, right on top of brotherly kindness?

cards.text: So why stack all that? Peter says if they have these qualities and keep growing in them, it makes a real difference in how they know our Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: If they keep growing in these qualities, those qualities will keep them from being ineffective and ___ in their knowledge of Jesus.

cards.text: But someone missing these traits, Peter says, is "nearsighted to the point of blindness". Strong words, friend.

cards.question: Peter says the person missing these traits has forgotten something. What?

answers.text: That he was cleansed from his past sins
That he once promised to follow God
That he still has work to finish

cards.text: Then Peter writes, "Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure." I was SURE I turned the oven off once, friend, and that batch came out a hockey puck.

cards.question: Peter says if they practice these things, they will ___ stumble.
Peter tells them what's waiting for them. What kind of welcome will they receive into the eternal kingdom of Jesus?
